A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAPO research and contain complete main text and Appendices A–C. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original experiments with six LLMs on synthetic problems, hotel reviews and variable tracking, including CoT evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds accuracy results and reasoning-token measurements for o3 and Gemini 2.5 Flash.

M1.justification: The prefix oracle, bounded attention, suffix oracle and autoregressive BAPO-CoT procedure are retained. Testing additional reasoning models does not introduce a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: Appendix C removes the numerical Min and Max evaluations. Other synthetic tasks, hotel reviews and variable tracking remain. MostNegativeReview becomes FindNegativeReview, but both versions use the same prompt and one-negative-among-positive-reviews sampling procedure.

E2.justification: Figure 4 substantially expands the central CoT comparison by adding o3 and Gemini 2.5 Flash, introducing models with internal reasoning alongside the six existing comparators. The original GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 and Gemini 1.5 variants remain.

E3.justification: The existing data-generation procedures, accuracy evaluation and 250-word CoT soft limit remain. Added experiments evaluate internal reasoning without an imposed token limit, specify medium reasoning effort for o3, and measure reasoning-token consumption.

E4.justification: New Figure 9 analyzes reasoning-token consumption across tasks and input lengths, examining the practical cost of CoT tractability. Min/Max CoT comparisons disappear; the representation and vocabulary-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 9 introduces box plots reporting variability in reasoning-token consumption. Accuracy reporting still specifies 100 i.i.d. instances and 95% t-test confidence intervals; no increase in repeated runs or new seed protocol is stated.

E6.justification: New Figure 4 results show o3 reaching approximately 100% on Reachability and Match3 and 84% on Majority at length 200; Gemini 2.5 Flash falls to roughly 40% on Majority. These are added model/budget results, not same-setting gains for existing models. Figure 9 adds token-consumption results, while Min/Max results are removed.

T1.justification: Table 1 corrects the trivial prefix bound from n ceil(log2 n) to n ceil(log2 |Sigma|), matching Section 2. The theorem statements and intended constructions remain. Theorem 7's proof introduces separate notation for original and growing inputs, but retains inconsistent n/m and x/y references.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an empirical contribution that o3 and Gemini 2.5 Flash perform well on BAPO-hard problems using many reasoning tokens. The effective-bandwidth hypothesis, hardness contributions and theoretical CoT tractability claim remain.

C2.justification: v3 changes the unchanged negative-review task's analogy from Min to Index/needle-in-a-haystack, adds a nearest-neighbor explanation of in-context learning, and attributes reasoning-model success to longer CoT and presumed training advantages. The labeled limitations mainly consolidate existing caveats.

D1.justification: The code-release placeholder becomes a concrete repository link. Appendix C adds reasoning-model versions/settings, runtime and API-cost estimates, and Space dataset access/license information. Min/Max prompts and generation details are removed with those evaluations.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gemini 2.5 Flash and o3/o4-mini release references, removes Meng et al. (2022) and the explicit mechanistic-interpretability contrast, and qualifies the discussion of Sanford et al.'s one-layer Match3 result. The broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Parts of the introduction, model explanation and discussion are rewritten; Section 4.2 and the negative-review task are renamed, and limitations receive a labeled paragraph. The main section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Empirical figures are broadly reformatted with side legends, resized plots and revised ticks. Figure 4 gains series and an expanded caption; a six-panel token-consumption figure is added. Min/Max panels disappear, four remaining appendix figures are consolidated onto one page, and the model-settings table gains rows and a parameter column.

improvement.justification: The reasoning-model results and token-cost analysis strengthen empirical support for the existing CoT theory, while concrete code access and additional implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. The gains are limited: model and budget changes do not isolate the proposed mechanism, Min/Max coverage is lost, and Theorem 7's notation revision is inconsistently applied.
